searchText: Not much, my library is the fastest of the libraries I'm aware of. Here are the libraries I know: https://github.com/guild-of-zk/pairing-bench/tree/master/vendor There are key low-level algortihm where you need a variable time for speed like inversion. For MSM too, but for pairings you don't really need it. Even compared with Gnark or MCL I'm faster. 4096 for KZG. I didn't optimize this one yet though. Focused on <512 and >16384 so far So that’s 40 ms per kzg batch single-threaded with the fastest library. Feels like JS impl perf would be too slow 🥶 I'll have to bench the wasm zprize single threaded. But wasm doesn't have "add-with-carry" and neither do MIPS or Risc, so they are really hindered for bigints. I plan to create a JIT compiler for targets like Nvidia/Intel/AMD GPUs and Wasm. Unfortunately using raw uint256 even when the compiler provides the intrinsics is too slow, see https://forum.nim-lang.org/t/10187#67460 I don't think the IR for zk I've seen so far (zkLLVM from Nil foundation, Zirgen from Riszc Zero, VampIR from Anoma) go so deep. I think there is 30% or so extra perf to get on GPUs or RiscZero VM or Optimism VM (cc <@203220829473996800> https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/cannon/wiki/Cannon-High-Level-Overview) And for an ISA to emulate I'm curious about the choice of RISC/MIPS vs the restricted ARM Thumbs-2 ISA. The Cannon wiki is outdated, see notice on wiki home page. I’ve been working on updating it to work on top of our next upgrade, and it’s getting faster too :). Also have been working on a RISC-V fault proof. That said, performance is less of an issue than ZK, since proof generation is already very viable on any machine, and onchain we bisect the work before doing a small proof of what’s left Fault proofs are different from fraud proof? It’s the same thing, but we don’t like calling it fraud proof, since it implies malicious behavior, whereas bugs can also cause differences in truth
